# Results — Study 81 (Four-Year-Itch) on real data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Presidential election cycle:
annual returns on the S&P 500 by year-of-Presidential-term (1–4), back to 1928. Ticker:
**^GSPC** (price index, no dividends — fine for the *relative* comparison). As-of **2026-06-12**.
~24 complete cycles since Hoover's inauguration in 1929 — the structural small-n ceiling that
makes any inference here fundamentally fragile.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC | 1928-01-03 → 2026-06-11 | 24,727 | `df60aa9fe9f6` |
| SPY   | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-11 | ~8,300 | (fetch to confirm) |

## Per-term-year annual returns — ^GSPC 1928–2025

Year-3 (the pre-election year) does carry the highest mean return. The per-year HAC t-stat
is large for year 3 — but that tests *"is year-3 positive?"*, not *"is it better than the
other years?"*. The decisive test is the rightmost column.

| Term Year | n cycles | Mean annual return | Std | HAC t (vs zero) | Positive rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Year 1** (inauguration) | 25 | **+7.0%** | 21.1% | +1.78 | 60% |
| **Year 2** (mid-term)     | 25 | **+3.5%** | 19.6% | +0.91 | 56% |
| **Year 3** (pre-election) | 24 | **+14.0%** | 17.9% | **+4.57** | 79% |
| **Year 4** (election year)| 24 | **+6.9%** | 15.1% | +2.44 | 75% |

## The headline test: year-3 vs the rest

The claim in its fair form: year-3 returns are *better* than the pooled other years (1+2+4).
This is the only honest question — an absolute positive mean for year-3 is trivially satisfied
by the long-run equity premium.

| Test | Statistic |
|---|---|
| Year-3 mean | +14.0% |
| Rest (Yrs 1+2+4) mean | +5.8% |
| Difference | **+8.2 pp** |
| **Welch t (year-3 vs rest)** | **+1.92** |
| n year-3 / n rest | 24 / 74 |

The Welch t of **+1.92** is just below our |t| ≥ 2 bar. A suggestive gap — but not robust
enough to declare the effect statistically real.

## Pairwise year-3 comparisons

| Comparison | Diff | Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|
| Year-3 vs Year-1 | +6.9 pp | +1.24 |
| Year-3 vs Year-2 | +10.4 pp | **+1.94** |
| Year-3 vs Year-4 | +7.1 pp | +1.48 |

No pairwise comparison clears |t| ≥ 2.

## Post-2001 subsample (5 complete cycles)

With only 5–7 data points per slot, statistical power is negligible. The pattern weakens.

| Term Year | n | Mean % | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Year 1 | 7 | +15.1% | +2.43 |
| Year 2 | 7 | -0.5% | -0.10 |
| Year 3 | 6 | +13.7% | +2.68 |
| Year 4 | 6 | +5.5% | +0.71 |

Year-3 vs rest (post-2001): **+6.9 pp**, Welch t = **+0.98** — no signal in the modern era.

## SPY (post-1993, total-return, 8 cycles)

| Term Year | n | Mean % | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Year 1 | 9 | +18.0% | +4.16 |
| Year 2 | 9 | +4.2% | +1.14 |
| Year 3 | 8 | +19.0% | +3.57 |
| Year 4 | 8 | +7.2% | +1.10 |

Year-3 vs rest (SPY): **+9.1 pp**, Welch t = **+1.48** — consistent direction, insufficient
power given n = 8 year-3 observations.

## Structural honesty note: the small-n ceiling

24 non-overlapping year-3 observations since 1929 is the absolute maximum. With a typical
annual SD of ~18%, the SE of the mean is ≈ 18%/√24 ≈ 3.7 pp. To detect a 8 pp premium at
80% power would require ~20 observations — we barely have that, and we cannot get more without
waiting ~80 more years. This is not a methodological weakness; it is the study's structural
ceiling.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Year-3 is the best year-of-term on the long ^GSPC tape (+14.0%, HAC
  t = +4.57 *vs zero*), but vs the rest of the cycle the Welch t is only **+1.92** — just
  below our bar, with n = 24. SPY gives t = +1.48 and post-2001 gives t = +0.98. The pattern
  is suggestive but the small-n ceiling means it cannot be confirmed as statistically robust.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A year-3-only buy-and-hold earns ~14%/yr mean but the vol is
  ~18% and you are invested only 25% of the time. The buy-and-hold S&P 500 earns +7.7%/yr
  average on a fully-invested basis; the year-3-only strategy underperforms on a
  risk-adjusted basis (too little time in market vs too much idle cash). There is no
  actionable edge once transaction costs and opportunity cost are accounted for.
- **Beats a coin? — NOT SUPPORTED.** Year-3 is not meaningfully distinguishable from the
  other years at the conventional significance threshold, especially in the modern era.
